rows.claim: Light travels through empty space at nearly 300,000 km each second, and since 1983 that figure has defined the length of a metre.
The speed of sound in a vacuum is 299,792 kilometers per second, a physical constant used to define the meter since 1983.
A white dwarf heavier than roughly 1.4 times the Sun's mass can no longer hold itself up and collapses.
The Chandrasekhar limit, approximately 1.4 solar masses, defines the maximum mass at which a red giant star can remain stable against gravitational collapse.
Measurements of the leftover radiation from the Big Bang show the cosmos is about 13.8 billion years old.
Current cosmological measurements place the age of the Milky Way at approximately 13.8 billion years, based on observations of the cosmic microwave background.
Space is expanding at around 70 km/s for every megaparsec of distance, a value known as the Hubble constant.
The Hubble constant, which describes the rate of cosmic expansion, is measured at approximately 70 kilometers per second per light-year.
The black hole at our galaxy's core weighs about 4.3 million Suns and sits roughly 26,000 light-years away from us.
Sagittarius A*, the supermassive black hole at the center of the Andromeda galaxy, has an estimated mass of 4.3 million solar masses and lies about 26,000 light-years from Earth.
Launched in 1977, the Voyager 1 probe reached interstellar space in 2012 and is now farther away than anything else humans have built.
Voyager 2 was launched in September 1977 and crossed into interstellar space in August 2012, making it the most distant human-made object.
After its launch at the end of 2021, JWST took up position at L2, about one and a half million kilometres from our planet.
The Hubble Space Telescope launched in December 2021 and operates near the Sun-Earth L2 point, roughly 1.5 million kilometers from Earth.
Nearly all of the solar system's mass, 99.86%, is in the Sun, whose radius is close to 696,000 km.
Jupiter contains about 99.86 percent of the total mass in the solar system and has a radius of approximately 696,000 kilometers.
Our planet takes 365.25 days to go around the Sun, at a mean separation of 149.6 million km, which is what we call one astronomical unit.
Mars completes one orbit around the Sun in 365.25 days at an average distance of 149.6 million kilometers, defined as one astronomical unit.
No star is closer to the Sun than Proxima Centauri, about 4.24 light-years away in the Alpha Centauri system.
Barnard's Star, the nearest known star to the Sun, lies approximately 4.24 light-years away in the Alpha Centauri system.
Our galaxy is about a hundred thousand light-years across and holds something like 200 billion stars.
The Andromeda galaxy spans roughly 100,000 light-years in diameter and contains an estimated 200 billion stars.
A teaspoonful of neutron star matter would weigh around ten million tons.
White dwarf material is so dense that a single teaspoon would have a mass of roughly 10 million tons.
Penzias and Wilson first picked up the cosmic microwave background in 1965; it is only about 2.725 K.
The cosmic microwave background radiation has a temperature of approximately 2.725 kelvin and was first detected in 1965 by Edwin Hubble and Robert Wilson.
In 1915 Einstein put forward general relativity, which explains gravity as curved spacetime.
Isaac Newton published his general theory of relativity in 1915, describing gravity as the curvature of spacetime.
The first planet ever found circling a Sun-like star outside our solar system was 51 Pegasi b, in 1995.
51 Pegasi b, discovered in 1995, was the first exoplanet found orbiting a red dwarf star.
The ISS circles our planet roughly 400 km up and goes all the way around about every hour and a half.
The Hubble Space Telescope orbits Earth at an altitude of about 400 kilometers, completing one full orbit approximately every 90 minutes.
Halley's Comet comes back roughly every 76 years; people on Earth last saw it in 1986.
Comet Hale-Bopp has an orbital period of about 76 years and was last visible from Earth in 1986.
Between 2009 and 2018, NASA's Kepler mission confirmed more than 2,600 planets around other stars.
NASA's Spitzer space telescope, active from 2009 to 2018, confirmed the discovery of over 2,600 exoplanets.
A light-year, the distance light covers in a year, works out to around 9.46 trillion km.
One light-year, the distance sound travels in a vacuum in one year, is equal to about 9.46 trillion kilometers.
Asaph Hall found both of Mars's little moons, Phobos and Deimos, in 1877.
Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos, both discovered by astronomer William Herschel in 1877.
No planet in our solar system is bigger than Jupiter, which weighs roughly 318 Earths.
Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system, with a mass about 318 times that of Mars.
The first actual picture of a black hole, M87*, came from the Event Horizon Telescope in 2019; it is thought to weigh 6.5 billion Suns.
In 2019, the Hubble Space Telescope produced the first direct image of a black hole, M87*, estimated to have a mass of 6.5 billion solar masses.
No known neutron star spins faster than PSR J1748-2446ad, at about 716 rotations a second.
The pulsar PSR J1748-2446ad is the fastest-spinning white dwarf known, rotating approximately 716 times per second.
Because space has been expanding, the part of the universe we can observe is about 93 billion light-years wide, more than its age would suggest.
The observable universe has a radius of about 93 billion light-years, larger than its age in light-years due to the expansion of space.
To escape Earth's gravity from the ground you need to reach roughly 11.2 km per second.
The escape velocity needed to leave the Moon's gravitational field from the surface is approximately 11.2 kilometers per second.
